spans.s: Adhidaiva (“the governing Deity,” see BR., vol. v, p. 971, and Weber, Rāmat. Up., 350): XII, 9175 (ºe niyukto 'smi, sc. Śiva).

Adhiratha, a sūta in the neighbourhood of Campā and friend of Dhṛtarāshṭra; husband of Rādhā and foster-father of Karṇa, whom he called Vasusheṇa and sent to Hāstinapura to be instructed by Droṇa (III, ch. 308); at the show of arms he enters the arena to congratulate Karṇa as king of Aṅga (I, ch. 137). § 218 (Astradarśana): 1, 137, 5419.-§ 547 (Kuṇḍalāharaṇap.): III, 309, 17153 (“the friend of Dhṛtarāshṭra”), 17157, 17168.--§ 572 (Rathātirath.): V, 166, 4759, 4762; 171, 4918.--§ 588 (Bhīshmavadhap.): VI, 122, 5826 (printed Ādhirathiḥ in C., but in B. Aºrathaḥ).
Adhivājyakulādyaḥ, a country. § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 352 (B.: Adhirājya-kuśādyaḥ; V.: Adhirājaṃ Kuśaṭṭāś ca); cf. VP. II, 165.
Adhivaṅga, a tīrtha. § 370 (Tīrthayātrāp.): III, 84, 8093 (tapovanam; B. tato vanam: the reward of visiting it is to rejoice among the Guhyakas).
